tracks.narration: Every program sees a clean slab of memory laid out the same way each time it runs.
At the bottom sits your code, frozen and read-only. Above it, the static data the compiler set up. The stack lives at the top — and the heap is everything in between.
Call malloc, and the heap creeps upward. Each new block sits wherever the allocator can find room.
Call a function, and a new frame is pushed onto the stack — locals, return address, the works. Return, and the frame is gone.
Two arrows, growing toward each other. As long as the gap holds, the program runs.
